=== _team.md ===
# Team



## Team name
The Prompt Engineers Who Can't Center a Div

## Our shared view on AI and the future of software engineering
AI agents are already good teammates for boilerplate, tests and first drafts, but they still need humans who understand the system, set the direction and check the result. We expect the job to shift from writing code to specifying, reviewing and verifying it. === harsh.md ===
# Harsh



## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science at Paderborn University; B.E. in Computer Engineering.

## Interests
Machine learning, football, and cooking dishes my mother would not approve of.

## Fun fact
I have more half-finished ML side projects than finished meals this semester.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
The models are surprisingly good at explaining code and writing tests, but they are weak at understanding why a system was built the way it was. They work best when the human brings the context.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Every developer will manage a small team of agents. Good engineers will be the ones who can break a problem into clear tasks and verify the results quickly.

## My hot take on AI
Most "AI bugs" are just human requirements that were never written down.

=== keval.md ===
# Keval



## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science at Paderborn University; B.E. in Computer Engineering.

## Interests
Cloud and DevOps, cricket, and long bike rides along the Lippe.

## Fun fact
My CI pipeline has a better success rate than my alarm clock.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is great for scripts, configs and debugging error messages, but it happily suggests insecure shortcuts. Security and operations still need a human who understands the risks.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Agents will deploy, monitor and fix systems on their own, so the real job will be setting the guardrails: permissions, tests and rollback plans.

## My hot take on AI
Giving an AI agent production access without a sandbox is just chaos engineering with extra steps.

=== krish.md ===
# Krish



## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science at Paderborn University; B.E. in Computer Engineering.

## Interests
Building side projects, cricket, and late-night debugging sessions with too much chai.

## Fun fact
I once fixed a production bug from my phone while waiting in a supermarket queue.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI assistants are great at boilerplate and first drafts, but they still need someone who understands the system to check their work. They speed me up most when I already know what I want.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Engineers will spend less time typing code and more time specifying, reviewing and testing what agents produce. Knowing *why* something should be built will matter more than knowing the syntax.

## My hot take on AI
The best prompt engineer on your team is just the person who writes the clearest tickets.

=== nevil.md ===
# Nevil



## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science at Paderborn University; B.E. in Computer Engineering.

## Interests
Frontend and UI design, photography, and badminton.

## Fun fact
I spend more time picking a colour palette than writing the actual code.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI can produce a working UI in minutes, but "working" and "pleasant to use" are not the same thing. It still needs a human eye for design, accessibility and the small details users notice.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Building software will feel more like directing than typing. Taste, user empathy and clear communication will matter more than knowing a framework.

## My hot take on AI
AI can center a div on the first try, which already makes it better than half of us.

=== nirav.md ===
# Nirav



## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science at Paderborn University; B.E. in Computer Engineering.

## Interests
Backend systems, table tennis, and trying every street food stall at a new place.

## Fun fact
I have named every one of my laptops after a Bollywood villain.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is a fast junior developer that never gets tired but also never says "I'm not sure". It saves me hours on boilerplate, but I still read every line before it goes anywhere near main.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Writing code will be the easy part. The hard part will be designing systems, defining what "correct" means and keeping agents from breaking each other's work.

## My hot take on AI
An AI that writes 1,000 lines a minute just means 1,000 lines a minute someone has to review.

---

Every team website MUST set the following metadata in the document head.

---

The page title MUST have the format:

    Team <group name> | Agentic SE Lab

Example: `Team Null Pointers | Agentic SE Lab`. Use a vertical bar, not a dash.
The group name in the title MUST match the group name shown in the page header.

observation:
[SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

---

[SG-21] Theme persistence (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Store the choice in `localStorage` under the key `theme`.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.

---

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

## Interests
Machine learning, football, and cooking dishes my mother would not approve of.

## Fun fact
I have more half-finished ML side projects than finished meals this semester.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

# Team



## Team name
The Prompt Engineers Who Can't Center a Div

## Our shared view on AI and the future of software engineering
AI agents are already good teammates for boilerplate, tests and first drafts, but they still need humans who understand the system, set the direction and check the result. We expect the job to shift from writing code to specifying, reviewing and verifying it. The engineers who do well will be the ones who can explain clearly what they want and notice quickly when the answer is wrong.

# Harsh



## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science at Paderborn University; B.E. in Computer Engineering.

## Interests
Machine learning, football, and cooking dishes my mother would not approve of.

## Fun fact
I have more half-finished ML side projects than finished meals this semester.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
The models are surprisingly good at explaining code and writing tests, but they are weak at understanding why a system was built the way it was. They work best when the human brings the context.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Every developer will manage a small team of agents. Good engineers will be the ones who can break a problem into clear tasks and verify the results quickly.

## My hot take on AI
Most "AI bugs" are just human requirements that were never written down.

[SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

[SG-21] Theme persistence (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Store the choice in `localStorage` under the key `theme`.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.

---

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

Observation:
[SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

---

[SG-21] Theme persistence (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Store the choice in `localStorage` under the key `theme`.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.

---

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

observation:
[SG-55] Motion and animation | Status: ACTIVE
Animations are allowed, but they must respect the user's settings.

- Transitions SHOULD be short (at most 300 ms). A smooth color transition when switching the theme is nice.
- If the page uses any `animation` or `transition`, it MUST include a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block
  that disables them.
- No autoplaying videos, no blinking or flashing elements.

---

[SG-01] Glossary | Status: ACTIVE
- **Team website**: the single HTML file that introduces one lab group.
- **Member card**: the block that introduces one team member.
- **Hot take**: a short, provocative opinion of a team member about AI.
- **Theme**: the visual mode of the page, either day (light) or night (dark).
- **Accent**: the one highlight color used for emphasis.
- **Breakpoint**: the viewport width at which the layout switches between mobile and desktop.
- **Data URI**: a way to embed a file (for example an image) directly inside the HTML.
- **Reduced motion**: a user setting in the operating system asking websites to minimise animation.

---

[SG-61] Navigation | Status: ACTIVE
- The header MAY contain a small navigation with links to the sections: `#team` and `#future-of-se`.
- On mobile, the navigation is shown below the tagline. Don't use a hamburger menu for two links.
- Use smooth scrolling only if reduced motion is not requested.

---

[SG-06] Tone of voice | Status: ACTIVE
Team websites are friendly, curious and a bit self-ironic.

- Write like you are explaining your team to other students at a coffee break.
- Prefer short sentences and active voice.
- Jokes are welcome, see the humor guidelines. Never make fun of other people or groups.
- Avoid marketing language like "revolutionary" or "game-changing", unless you are clearly joking.
- Opinions about AI SHOULD be honest. It is fine to be sceptical.

# Team



## Team name
The Prompt Engineers Who Can't Center a Div

## Our shared view on AI and the future of software engineering
AI agents are already good teammates for boilerplate, tests and first drafts, but they still need humans who understand the system, set the direction and check the result. ## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science at Paderborn University; B.E. in Computer Engineering.

## Interests
Machine learning, football, and cooking dishes my mother would not approve of.

## Fun fact
I have more half-finished ML side projects than finished meals this semester.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
The models are surprisingly good at explaining code and writing tests, but they are weak at understanding why a system was built the way it was. They work best when the human brings the context.

Every developer will manage a small team of agents. Good engineers will be the ones who can break a problem into clear tasks and verify the results quickly.

## My hot take on AI
Most "AI bugs" are just human requirements that were never written down.

No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

Observation:
[SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

---

[SG-21] Theme persistence (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Store the choice in `localStorage` under the key `theme`.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.

---

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.

- **Team website**: the single HTML file that introduces one lab group.

- **Breakpoint**: the viewport width at which the layout switches between mobile and desktop.

[SG-03] Single-file delivery | Status: ACTIVE
Team websites are delivered as exactly one HTML file.

- All CSS MUST be inside `<style>` elements, all JavaScript inside `<script>` elements.
- The page MUST NOT load anything from the network: no CDNs, no web fonts, no external images, no analytics.
- Images MUST be embedded as data URIs (base64).
- The file SHOULD stay below 8 MB. Compress photos before embedding them (around 400 × 400 pixels is enough).
- The page MUST work when opened directly from the file system (file://).

---

[SG-59] Frequently asked questions | Status: ACTIVE
**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

---

[SG-29] Links | Status: ACTIVE
- Links are shown in the accent color and underlined.
- External links (for example to GitHub profiles) MAY be used, because they don't load resources.
- External links SHOULD open in the same tab.

---

[SG-56] Performance | Status: ACTIVE
- The page SHOULD render in under one second on a laptop.
- Keep JavaScript small; the theme toggle needs only a few lines.
- Resize photos before embedding them. A 5 MB phone photo turns into almost 7 MB of base64 text.

[SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

---

[SG-21] Theme persistence (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Store the choice in `localStorage` under the key `theme`.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.

---

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

[SG-03] Single-file delivery | Status: ACTIVE
Team websites are delivered as exactly one HTML file.

- All CSS MUST be inside `<style>` elements, all JavaScript inside `<script>` elements.
- The page MUST NOT load anything from the network: no CDNs, no web fonts, no external images, no analytics.
- Images MUST be embedded as data URIs (base64).
- The file SHOULD stay below 8 MB. Compress photos before embedding them (around 400 × 400 pixels is enough).
- The page MUST work when opened directly from the file system (file://).

[SG-59] Frequently asked questions | Status: ACTIVE
**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

AI agents are already good teammates for boilerplate, tests and first drafts, but they still need humans who understand the system, set the direction and check the result. [SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

---

[SG-21] Theme persistence (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Store the choice in `localStorage` under the key `theme`.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.

---

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

Animations are allowed, but they must respect the user's settings.

[SG-01] Glossary | Status: ACTIVE
- **Team website**: the single HTML file that introduces one lab group.
- **Member card**: the block that introduces one team member.
- **Hot take**: a short, provocative opinion of a team member about AI.
- **Theme**: the visual mode of the page, either day (light) or night (dark).
- **Accent**: the one highlight color used for emphasis.
- **Breakpoint**: the viewport width at which the layout switches between mobile and desktop.
- **Data URI**: a way to embed a file (for example an image) directly inside the HTML.
- **Reduced motion**: a user setting in the operating system asking websites to minimise animation.

[SG-03] Single-file delivery | Status: ACTIVE
Team websites are delivered as exactly one HTML file.

- All CSS MUST be inside `<style>` elements, all JavaScript inside `<script>` elements.
- The page MUST NOT load anything from the network: no CDNs, no web fonts, no external images, no analytics.
- Images MUST be embedded as data URIs (base64).
- The file SHOULD stay below 8 MB. Compress photos before embedding them (around 400 × 400 pixels is enough).
- The page MUST work when opened directly from the file system (file://).

---

[SG-59] Frequently asked questions | Status: ACTIVE
**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

- Resize photos before embedding them. A 5 MB phone photo turns into almost 7 MB of base64 text.

# Team

## Our shared view on AI and the future of software engineering
AI agents are already good teammates for boilerplate, tests and first drafts, but they still need humans who understand the system, set the direction and check the result. [SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

---

[SG-21] Theme persistence (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Store the choice in `localStorage` under the key `theme`.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.

---

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

[SG-03] Single-file delivery | Status: ACTIVE
Team websites are delivered as exactly one HTML file.

- Images MUST be embedded as data URIs (base64).

[SG-59] Frequently asked questions | Status: ACTIVE
**Can we use Google Fonts?**
No. Fonts are loaded from the network, which breaks single-file delivery.

**Our old site used a black night mode. Is that still ok?**
No, the night palette changed in version 2 of the guide.

**Can we use Bootstrap or Tailwind?**
Not from a CDN. You'd have to inline all of it, which makes the file huge. Plain CSS is enough.

**What breakpoint should we use?**
The breakpoint changed in version 3. Always check the ACTIVE responsive document.

**One member doesn't want a photo online. What now?**
Use an avatar or a drawing. The alt text then says "Avatar of <first name>".

**Can we add more sections?**
Yes, as long as the required sections exist, see the page structure document.

[SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

[SG-21] Theme persistence (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example

- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.

- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

[SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

---

[SG-21] Theme persistence (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Store the choice in `localStorage` under the key `theme`.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.

---

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

# Team



## Team name
The Prompt Engineers Who Can't Center a Div

## Our shared view on AI and the future of software engineering
AI agents are already good teammates for boilerplate, tests and first drafts, but they still need humans who understand the system, set the direction and check the result. We expect the job to shift from writing code to specifying, reviewing and verifying it. The engineers who do well will be the ones who can explain clearly what they want and notice quickly when the answer is wrong.

Machine learning, football, and cooking dishes my mother would not approve of.

## Fun fact
I have more half-finished ML side projects than finished meals this semester.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
The models are surprisingly good at explaining code and writing tests, but they are weak at understanding why a system was built the way it was. They work best when the human brings the context.

Every developer will manage a small team of agents. Good engineers will be the ones who can break a problem into clear tasks and verify the results quickly.

## My hot take on AI
Most "AI bugs" are just human requirements that were never written down.

[SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

[SG-21] Theme persistence (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Store the choice in `localStorage` under the key `theme`.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.

---

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.
